items.title: Diamond Power Infrastructure among 3 stocks that closed above VWAP
items.description: On October 8, the closing prices of three stocks in the Nifty 500 pack were above their respective Volume Weighted Average Prices (VWAPs), according to StockEdge technical scan data.When the closing price is above the VWAP, it means the stock closed at a price higher than its volume-weighted average traded price during the day. The VWAP gives greater weight to prices at which higher trading volumes occurred.

items.title: TCS shares jump 4% after Q2 results. What are Goldman Sachs, Nomura, others saying?
items.description: TCS shares surged after the IT major reported a 15% year-on-year rise in Q2 consolidated net profit to Rs 13,884 crore. Revenue in constant currency terms grew 0.5% quarter-on-quarter, while operating margin stood at 24%. The company declared a second interim dividend of Rs 12 per share for FY27.

items.title: Sensex jumps 500 points, Nifty above 22,400 a day after crash as Trump rules out Iran strikes. What lies ahead?
items.description: The Indian stock market experienced a positive start, bouncing back from previous significant losses. Contributing to this recovery were lower oil prices following recent sharp declines. The Nifty IT sector particularly excelled, though broader market performance was mixed. Analysts express caution regarding how elevated crude prices and high US bond yields could shape future trading dynamics. For patient long-term investors, this market correction may present favorable buying opportunities.

items.title: ITC shares in focus after Rajiv Jain-backed GQG sells stake worth Rs 9,395 crore. What’s ahead after 30% crash in 2026
items.description: ITC shares will be in focus after Rajiv Jain-backed GQG sold shares worth Rs 9,395 crore, reducing its stake amid a sharp stock decline. Cigarette tax hikes, inflation and rising oil prices weighed on performance. Investors now await quarterly earnings, while brokerages remain divided on the stock’s outlook and valuation prospects.

items.title: ITC among 4 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of October 8, four stocks in the NSE F&O segment recorded a rise of more than 10% in futures open interest compared with the previous trading session, according to StockEdge F&O scan data. A notable increase in futures open interest indicates a substantial rise in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a security. This may reflect market participants initiating new positions or increasing the size of their existing positions.

items.title: Infosys, TCS, Wipro and other IT stocks rise up to 4%. Here are 3 important triggers to watch
items.description: IT stocks including TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Tech Mahindra, Coforge and Persistent Systems rose up to 4% on Friday. The gains came amid a confluence of factors, including second-quarter earnings and the US suspension of a certification programme. TCS and Wipro were among the key gainers, while midcap IT stocks also saw strong buying interest during the session.

items.title: Firstsource Solutions among 4 stocks showing RSI trending up
items.description: On October 8, four Nifty500 stocks appeared in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on StockEdge data.The scan identifies stocks whose RSI values have crossed above 50 from below, indicating strengthening momentum. The Relative Strength Index is a technical indicator commonly used by traders to assess price momentum and trend strength.

items.title: KPR Mill among 4 stocks closing below VWAP
items.description: On October 8, the closing prices of four stocks from the Nifty 500 pack fell more than 2% below their respective VWAPs (Volume Weighted Average Prices), according to StockEdge’s technical scan data.VWAP represents the average price at which a stock traded during the day, weighted by trading volume. A closing price below VWAP indicates that the stock ended the session below its volume-weighted average traded price.

items.title: India IT set for fourth year of weak growth on geopolitics, AI risks
items.description: As HCL Technologies Ltd. and Tech Mahindra Ltd. unveil their latest reports, investors are keenly observing the situation, particularly given the looming threats posed by AI disruptions and restrained client expenditures. These factors are influencing growth forecasts for tech companies. Tata Consultancy Services Ltd. did exceed expectations in profit gains; however, revenue growth remained modest in terms of constant currency.

items.title: Negative Breakout: These 8 stocks cross below their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, eight stocks' closing prices crossed below their 200-day moving averages (DMA) on October 08, according to technical scan data from StockEdge. Trading below the 200 DMA is generally considered a negative signal, as it suggests that a stock’s price is below its long-term trend. The 200 DMA is a widely used technical indicator that helps traders assess the overall trend of a stock.

items.title: Rising oil, weak rupee and rate fears hammer Dalal Street; VIX jumps 10%
items.description: On Thursday, Indian equities faced a significant sell-off, leading to declines in both Sensex and Nifty. The Sensex dropped by 1,045.46 points, while Nifty fell by 371.25 points. The decline resulted in a market capitalisation loss of nearly ₹10 lakh crore. Global concerns such as elevated oil prices and interest rate increases are impacting investor sentiment. Overall, the Indian stock market continues to struggle amid challenging economic factors.

items.title: Weak rains clouds recovery in Rs 3.3 lakh crore microfinance sector
items.description: India's microfinance sector, with a market worth ₹3.30 lakh crore, is encountering credit risk hurdles. Key factors include inconsistent rainfall and drought in critical states such as Karnataka and Maharashtra, which deeply influence the agricultural economy tied to rural borrowers. In response, some institutions are exercising caution by closely monitoring high-risk areas, yet the lack of loan protection further exacerbates the financial risks involved.

items.title: Vedanta announces Rs 5 per share dividend, sets October 14 as record date
items.description: Vedanta has announced a dividend of ₹5 per share for the current fiscal, which will amount to a total payout of ₹1,955 crore from the company. Record date for the dividend is October 14. This is the first dividend announced by the company this fiscal, and effectively, the first after its mega demerger in June.

items.title: Jane Street hits back at Sebi’s allegations, says ‘regulator changed the goal posts’
items.description: Jane Street's counsel challenged the Securities and Exchange Board of India's claims regarding its trading strategy and actions. The firm has paid the amount requested by SEBI, even before a hearing took place. Jane Street halted its trading in India and questioned the regulator's focus on large trade volumes. Complaints received by SEBI were discussed, emphasizing the right to know the complainants' identities.

items.title: Stocks in news: TCS, ITC, Infosys, Cochin Shipyard and RIL
items.description: On Thursday, the financial markets took a hit, plummeting by almost 1.5% due to robust selling pressure. The Nifty index wavered near its April 2026 low, suggesting ongoing vulnerabilities. In a positive twist, TCS announced a notable 15% rise in its consolidated net profit for the second quarter. Meanwhile, ITC engaged in a substantial block trade, while shares of Infosys and Wipro faced declines during US market hours.

items.title: D-Street poised for positive start as GIFT Nifty signals gains
items.description: Benchmark indices encountered significant pressure as both US bond yields and crude oil prices climbed above $104 per barrel. Foreign portfolio investors sold equities amounting to Rs 12,943 crore while domestic investors acquired Rs 10,703 crore in shares. Analysts express concerns that potential breaches of support levels might lead to further market declines.

items.title: Cupid among 7 stocks that hit 52-week highs; rallied up to 30% in a month
items.description: On Friday, the benchmark Sensex surged 879 points to close at 72,472. Amid the rally, seven stocks from the BSE 1000 index touched fresh 52-week highs, reaching their highest price levels in the past year. A 52-week high marks the highest price at which a stock has traded over the previous 12 months and can indicate strong buying interest.

items.title: Nomura becomes latest brokerage to cut PB Fintech share price target by 31%, lists 2 scenarios for fair price
items.description: Nomura has cut PB Fintech’s target price by 31% to Rs 1,100 after proposed IRDAI curbs on insurance website practices and commissions. The brokerage lowered earnings estimates, while alternative scenarios suggest fair values of Rs 1,335-1,366.

items.title: Friday heavy lifting saves Nifty from record nine weeks of losses. Can bulls take charge now?
items.description: Nifty broke its eight-week losing streak, rising nearly 1.3% on Friday to close above 22,500 as IT, FMCG and auto stocks led a relief rally. However, persistent FII selling, elevated US bond yields, crude oil prices and the RBI’s shift to calibrated tightening continue to cloud the market outlook.

items.title: Madhusudan Kela-backed MV Electrosystems shares more than double from IPO price in just 2 months. Should you buy?
items.description: MV Electrosystems shares have surged over 100% from their IPO price, boosting Madhuri Kela’s stake value to Rs 111.55 crore. However, declining FY26 revenue and a net loss raise concerns about the company’s future profitability.

items.title: Rs 1,024-crore market cap, Rs 10,000-crore order book: This penny stock jumps 11% after SAIL deal
items.description: SEPC shares jumped nearly 11% to Rs 5.47 on Friday after securing an Rs 854.57-crore contract from SAIL for its IISCO Steel Plant expansion in Burnpur. The deal pushes SEPC's consolidated order book past Rs 10,000 crore, nearly 10 times its market capitalisation, providing multi-year revenue visibility.

items.title: How Do Family Offices Hunt for Multibagger Startups?
items.description: At the ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0, family office leaders discuss what it takes to identify the next multibagger startup, drawing on their experience of backing companies such as Zomato and Flipkart early on. They also explain why tracking the US as the “mother market” can help investors spot global trends and identify emerging opportunities in India.

items.title: Ashish Kacholia sells over 2 lakh Carysil shares in Q2. How has the stock fared?
items.description: Ace investor Ashish Kacholia trimmed his stake in Carysil by over 2 lakh shares during the July-September quarter of FY27, reducing his holding to 2.72%. The kitchen sink maker’s stock has corrected sharply from its July peak after a strong rally earlier this year. Here’s a look at Carysil’s recent share price performance, long-term returns and analyst outlook.

items.title: 6 Defence stocks turn multibaggers in H1 FY27, rally up to 600%
items.description: While Indian equities remained volatile, delivering largely negative or flat returns in the first half of FY27, the Nifty India Defence index emerged as a standout performer, rallying 25%. Within the defence pack, 10 stocks posted impressive gains ranging from 50% to nearly 600%. Notably, six of these stocks turned multibaggers, more than doubling investors’ wealth in just over six months of FY27, making them some of the sector’s biggest gainers, according to ACE Equity data.

items.title: Pidilite shares rise marginally as company appoints Amit Agarwal CFO-designate
items.description: Pidilite Industries shares rose on Friday after the company appointed Amit Agarwal as CFO-designate and Senior Management Personnel, effective October 9, 2026. Agarwal brings over 22 years of finance experience and has previously worked with Pfizer, Hindustan Unilever and Vedanta Resources. He is a Chartered Accountant, Cost Accountant and Company Secretary.

items.title: Explained: Why IT stocks ignored Donald Trump’s PERM suspension to gain Rs 70,000 crore in one day
items.description: IT stocks rallied up to 4% on Friday, adding Rs 70,000 crore in market capitalisation, despite the US suspension of a labour certification programme. Strong Q2 results from TCS, easing oil prices and bond yields, and developments around OpenAI also supported sentiment. TCS gained after reporting 15% profit growth, while brokerages flagged near-term margin pressures and evolving AI-related risks.

items.title: Vedanta shares jump over 3% after Rs 5 interim dividend announcement
items.description: Vedanta shares rose on Friday after the mining major announced its first interim dividend of Rs 5 per share for FY27, with a total payout of Rs 1,955 crore. The dividend marks the company's first since its demerger into five entities, which could reshape its future dividend payouts.

items.title: Vivriti Asset Management returns over Rs 3,400 crore to investors across two fund vintages
items.description: Vivriti Asset Management has completed and exited its Vintage II credit funds, returning over Rs 2,260 crore in capital and income. The funds invested across more than 45 companies, delivering gross IRRs of around 12% to 15%.

items.title: 15,410% rally in 5 years! Multibagger Cupid shares jump 3% to hit fresh 52-week high
items.description: Cupid shares jumped hit a fresh 52-week high of Rs 368 on Friday, extending their rally for a fourth straight session. Earlier this month, Cupid raised its FY27 revenue and profit guidance for the second time in less than two weeks, targeting revenue of Rs 800 crore and net profit of Rs 250 crore for the financial year.

items.title: Apollo, Max Health, other hospital stocks rally up to 5% despite cancer drug price caps. Why Jefferies stays bullish
items.description: Hospital stocks rose up to 5% after the government capped trade margins on non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs at 30%, potentially reducing medicine prices by 70%. Jefferies and Emkay expect manageable earnings impacts, despite near-term margin pressures. Jefferies favours Fortis, Manipal, Apollo, Max Healthcare and Medanta, citing strong demand and attractive valuations.

items.title: Hexaware Technologies shares surge 11% on multi-year pact with Anthropic
items.description: Hexaware Technologies shares surged after the IT services firm announced a multi-year partnership with Anthropic to integrate its Claude AI models into its platforms. The tie-up will focus on enterprise AI solutions and deployments across IT operations and software engineering.

items.title: Rs 30 lakh crore wiped out! What will it take for bulls to recover from a 6-week selling rut?
items.description: The Indian stock market has undergone a significant downturn, with nearly Rs 30 lakh crore wiped off its market capitalisation. Contributing factors include surging oil prices and elevated bond yields. Experts predict that any potential rebound hinges on the health of the broader economy. Additionally, Foreign Institutional Investors have been notably offloading their equities, while technical indicators display a cautious outlook as Nifty struggles against ongoing bearish trends.

items.title: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 30% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: Keep a close watch on updates from FMCG companies, the cement sector, from real estate companies, especially about the commercial segment of those focused on South India. What they say will provide an idea of how things are panning out on the ground.

items.title: Anthem Biosciences block deal: Portsmouth Technologies sells 30 lakh shares worth Rs 250 crore
items.description: Portsmouth Technologies LLC executed a block deal selling 30 lakh shares of Anthem Biosciences on October 9. The shares were sold at Rs 833 each, totaling Rs 249.90 crore. Following this transaction, Portsmouth's estimated stake in the company would decrease significantly. Anthem Biosciences reported a decline in total income and profit after tax for the first quarter of FY27.

items.title: Half of India’s MTF book is in smallcaps; Nithin Kamath flags liquidity risks
items.description: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath warned that small and microcap stocks account for a substantial share of India’s margin trading facility book. He highlighted liquidity risks during market downturns, when smaller stocks may face sharper selling pressure.

items.title: Adani Power shares: GQG Partners-managed entities cut stake to 5.72% from 5.74%
items.description: GQG Partners entities sold 50.39 lakh Adani Power shares through on-market transactions, reducing their combined stake to 5.72% from 5.74%. The disclosure comes as the stock gains 27.05% in 2026 and the company expands into Bhutanese hydropower.

items.title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0 | SIFs, passive funds and GIFT City: How India's wealth portfolios are evolving, says Tata AMC's Anand Vardarajan
items.description: Tata Asset Management CEO Anand Vardarajan highlights how passive funds, SIFs and GIFT City are reshaping wealth management. He advocates combining active and passive strategies while monitoring global yields, inflation and valuations to build diversified portfolios.

items.title: Market wrap: ITC, TCS, BSE, RIL top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Friday
items.description: The Indian equity markets saw a robust recovery as both the BSE Sensex and Nifty 50 registered remarkable gains. The Nifty 50 surged by 288.65 points, closing at 22,520.45, while the Sensex jumped 879.09 points. Notably, the Nifty IT index rose 3%, signaling a positive market sentiment. A total of 2,182 out of 3,684 stocks climbed higher, reflecting renewed investor interest in bargain opportunities.
